item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
017
ABPZ20 KNHC 291747
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located just inland in Sonora, Mexico, on Hurricane Nolo,
located several hundred miles west-southwest of Lihue, Hawaii, on
Tropical Storm Rachel, located a few hundred miles southwest of
Lazaro Cardenas, Mexico, and on newly formed Tropical Depression
Nineteen-E, located over the western East Pacific.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form late this week or this weekend to
the south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter, environmental
conditions appear favorable for gradual development while the system
moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ34 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Nineteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ24 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Tropical Storm Polo Public Advisory Number 37
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 292036
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Polo Advisory Number  37
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
200 PM MST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
...POLO WEAKENS TO A TROPICAL STORM AS IT MOVES FARTHER INLAND...
...STRONG WINDS AND HEAVY RAINS SPREADING ACROSS NORTHWESTERN
MEXICO TOWARD SOUTHERN NEW MEXICO AND FAR WESTERN TEXAS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.0N 109.7W
ABOUT 100 MI...160 KM NE OF GUAYMAS MEXICO
ABOUT 275 MI...445 KM SW OF EL PASO TEXAS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NE OR 40 DEGREES AT 21 MPH...33 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...992 MB...29.30 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has discontinued all coastal warnings and
watches.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in northwestern Mexico, southern New Mexico, and far
western Texas should continue to monitor the progress of Polo.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Polo was
located near latitude 29.0 North, longitude 109.7 West. Polo is now
moving toward the northeast near 21 mph (33 km/h) and this motion is
expected to continue with an additional increase in forward speed 
through tonight. On the forecast track, the center of Polo will 
cross northwestern Mexico this afternoon and evening before 
dissipating. The remnants of Polo should continue quickly 
northeastward, passing over southern New Mexico and far western 
Texas late tonight or early Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Rapid weakening is expected as the center of Polo moves
farther inland, and the surface circulation is expected to
dissipated tonight. However, the remnants of Polo are likely bring
gusty winds to portions of southern New Mexico and far western Texas
late tonight and early Tuesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60 miles (95 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 992 mb (29.30 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are spreading across northwestern
Mexico near the center of Polo and will continue spread 
northeastward tonight.
 
A Wind Advisory is in effect for portions of southern New Mexico and
far western Texas where strong gusty winds are possible late today
and tonight in association with Polo’s remnants. Refer to products
issued by your local National Weather Service Forecast Office for
additional information.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 6
inches across southern and central portions of Sonora with isolated
maximum totals of 8 inches. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will continue to affect portions of
the coast of the Baja California peninsula and northwestern Mexico
during the next day or so. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Polo Forecast Discussion Number 37
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 292037
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Polo Discussion Number  37
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
200 PM MST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
Since the last advisory, Polo has moved northeastward across the 
Gulf of California and made landfall in the Mexican state of Sonora 
just east of Guaymas.  The cyclone is now weakening as it moves 
farther inland and it is estimated that it is now a 55-kt 
tropical storm. Rapid weakening is expected as Polo crosses 
northwestern Mexico, and it is likely that the surface circulation 
will dissipate tonight. A 12-h position is included in this 
advisory, but it is likely to be the position of a trough or 
vorticity maximum and not a circulation center.

The initial motion is now 040/18. Polo and its remnants are expected 
to move rapidly northeastward through Wednesday in the flow on the 
east side of a mid-latitude trough over the southwestern United 
States. This track will bring the system across northwestern Mexico 
and into portions of New Mexico and Texas as it interacts with the 
trough. This evolution will contribute to heavy rainfall, flash 
flooding, and gusty winds in the southwestern U.S. and southern 
Plains. See products issued by the Weather Prediction Center and 
local National Weather Service offices for more information.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across 
northwestern Mexico near the center of Polo through tonight.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will continue to impact the 
southern and central portions of Sonora today. This rainfall is 
expected to produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, 
especially in areas of steep terrain. Moisture from Polo will 
support heavy rainfall and flooding potential across the Southwest 
U.S. into the Southern High Plains today into early Wednesday.
 
3. Even after the surface circulation of Polo dissipates, its low- 
to mid-level remnants may produce strong gusty winds well inland 
over the higher terrain of northwest Mexico, southern New Mexico, 
and far western Texas.
 
4. Dangerous surf and rip currents are likely to persist along 
portions of the northwest coast of Mexico and Baja California for 
the next day or so.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  30/0600Z 32.6N 105.7W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 24H  30/1800Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.description:
Issued at 1200 PM CST Tue Sep 29 2026 
371 
WTPZ33 KNHC 291749
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Intermediate Advisory Number 10A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
1200 PM CST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
...RACHEL HOLDING STEADY SOUTH OF SOUTHWESTERN MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 PM CST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.7N 105.1W
ABOUT 250 MI...400 KM SW OF LAZARO CARDENAS MEXICO
ABOUT 325 MI...525 KM S OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...987 MB...29.15 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Coast of southwestern Mexico from Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Coast of southwestern Mexico north of Playa Perula to Cabo
Corrientes
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 PM CST (1800 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was 
located by NOAA Hurricane Hunter Reconnaissance aircraft near 
latitude 15.7 North, longitude 105.1 West. Rachel is moving toward 
the northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h). A northwestward motion at a 
slower forward speed is expected during the next several days. On 
the forecast track, the center of Rachel is predicted to move 
parallel to, but stay offshore of, the coast of southwestern 
Mexico. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual strengthening is expected during the next few days, 
and Rachel is forecast to become a hurricane later today. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 miles (260 km)
from the center.
 
The minimum central pressure estimated from the NOAA Hurricane 
Hunter aircraft data is 987 mb (29.15 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected in the warning area
later today or tonight. Tropical storm conditions are possible in
the watch area by tonight or Wednesday.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches, with isolated maximum totals of 12 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero, Michoacán, Colima and
Jalisco. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect portions of the
southwestern coast of Mexico during the next couple of days and
spread northward through the end of the week. These swells are
likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 291452
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
900 AM CST Tue Sep 29 2026
 
Rachel is dealing with around 20 kt of northeasterly wind shear this 
morning, with the estimated center position located along the far 
northern edge of the central dense overcast. However, a burst of 
deep convection, with cloud top temperatures of around -90 C, along 
with strong upper-level outflow suggests that the system is slowly 
intensifying. The latest TAFB Dvorak intensity estimate was 3.5/55 
kt, while recent objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range 
from 43-55 kt. Given the deepening convection and the slight 
increase in intensity estimates, the initial intensity is set at 55 
kt for this advisory. 
 
The strong tropical storm is moving toward the west-northwest around 
11 kt, steered by a strong mid-level ridge centered over the 
south-central United States. A turn toward the northwest is expected 
later today as high pressure builds over eastern Mexico, followed by 
a gradual decrease in forward speed as Rachel moves into a region 
with weaker steering flow. By late week, building high pressure to 
the northwest of the cyclone should induce a gradual turn back 
toward the west-northwest and then west, accompanied by a slight 
increase in forward speed. The updated forecast track is very 
similar to the previous advisory, remaining near the middle of the 
track forecast guidance envelope through 48 h and near the northern 
end of the guidance thereafter. 
 
Decreasing wind shear, sufficiently warm sea surface temperatures 
and favorable upper-level divergence are expected to support 
strengthening over the next couple of days, and Rachel is forecast 
to become a hurricane later today. However, Rachel could briefly 
move over slightly cooler waters left in the wake of Hurricane Polo 
tonight into early Wednesday, which may temporarily limit the rate 
of intensification. Thereafter, warmer waters should support 
additional strengthening through late this week. The latest NHC 
intensity forecast is near the upper-end of the guidance envelope, 
although it remains slightly below the HCCA solution. 
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Although the core of Rachel is forecast to remain offshore of 
Mexico, tropical-storm-force winds are expected along a portion of 
the coast of southwestern Mexico in the Tropical Storm Warning area 
today or tonight. Tropical storm conditions are possible in the 
watch area tonight or on Wednesday.
 
2. Outer bands from Rachel will bring locally heavy rainfall to
portions of coastal southwest Mexico through Thursday. This rainfall
may produce areas of flooding and mudslides, especially in regions
of steep terrain.
 
3. Large waves could produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along portions of the southwestern coast of Mexico during
the next several days.

item.description:

...TROPICAL DEPRESSION NINETEEN MOVING SLOWLY EASTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.2N 130.8W
ABOUT 1490 MI...2400 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...E OR 90 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Nineteen-E was located near latitude 14.2 North, longitude 130.8
West. The depression is moving toward the east near 7 mph (11 km/h)
and this motion is expected to continue over the next few days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast during the next couple of 
days, and this system is expected to degenerate into a 
post-tropical cyclone by Thursday. 
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.

item.title: Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 292034
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Depression Nineteen-E Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP192026
200 PM PDT Tue Sep 29 2026

Tropical Depression Nineteen's convection has dwindled quite a bit 
over the last several hours. The system's low-level center remains 
completely exposed, with lingering convective activity lying several 
dozen miles to the north of the circulation. Scatterometry data from 
this afternoon just clipped the storm's eastern flank, so TD 19's 
initial intensity will hedge more towards TAFB's latest Dvorak 
estimate of 2.0/30 kt, remaining steady from the last advisory.

Satellite imagery suggests that forward speed has slowed as well, 
with the initial motion set at 85/6 kt. The depression is generally 
expected to remain on an eastward trajectory as it is steered by a 
northward-displaced equatorial trough. Little was changed in the 
track forecast from the previous advisory, as models are largely in 
good agreement on the storm's path. Only slight adjustments in 
forward speed were made to better follow current trends. 

Several environmental factors will inhibit further development of 
the depression. Moderate vertical wind shear, drying mid-level air, 
and marginal SSTs left in the wake of the remnants of Odalys are 
likely to keep the system from reaching tropical storm strength. 
Diurnal convection cycles may allow the system to briefly flirt with 
tropical storm strength, however simulated satellite imagery across 
global models depict little to no convection for this system over 
the next 48 h. The latest intensity forecast moves up the 
depression's post-tropical transition time to Thursday afternoon, 
and dissipation is forecast shortly thereafter.
